assumptions: Invited NVIDIA architecture paper; detailed interposer/ring-link values are simulations, selected demonstrations or design targets. Its 800 Gb/s/fibre and 28-45 Gb/s/channel results are not 200G/400G-per-lane scale-out engine results.
limitations: No production interposer, complete 102.4T/204.8T system, final yield, thermal qualification, fibre-attach process, customer deployment, cost, ASP, margin or foundry/OSAT ownership evidence.
relevance: Roadmap and value-chain boundary reference for accelerator optical I/O and possible post-CPO migration; not a current company-leadership result.
notes: DOI: 10.1109/JLT.2022.3219379. Full 11-page PDF text-extracted and title page visually verified on 2026-08-07.

title: Exploring the benefits of using co-packaged optics in data center and AI supercomputer networks: a simulation-based analysis
author: Pavlos Maniotis and Daniel M. Kuchta
organisation: Journal of Optical Communications and Networking
technology_area: CPO; AI networks; switch radix; topology; network locality; simulation
main_claim: IBM's discrete-event models find higher-radix CPO configurations can reduce switch count and improve locality/throughput under specified traffic and topology assumptions.
important_numbers: Modeled 100T CPO network: 64% fewer switches (48 vs 132); >90% higher mean server throughput for 256 nodes and messages >=128 KiB. Data-center model: 41% fewer switches (160 vs 272); up to 68% higher completion time when applications span switches at a 1.25 us stack latency.
assumptions: Simulated topology, traffic, latency and hardware assumptions; CPO at both switch and accelerator points for the 100T comparison.
limitations: No hardware deployment, product cost, yield, field reliability, commercial adoption or verified system power; results cannot be attributed to a public company.
relevance: Strong mechanism evidence that higher radix/locality can be a CPO adoption driver beyond optical power.
notes: Full 14-page PDF visually inspected and text-extracted. DOI: 10.1364/JOCN.501427. Use all numerical results as simulations, not market forecasts.

title: 100G and 200G per Lane Linear Drive Optics for Data Center Applications
author: Elaine S. Chou et al.
technology_area: LPO; 100G per lane; 200G per lane; electrical loss; retimers
main_claim: 100G LPO is measured in a 51.2T switch; the 200G result is a model that requires about 22-23 dB loss for the stated linear-drive limits and a Tx retimer for the paper's longer planned path.
important_numbers: 100G: up to 15 dB at 26 GHz; most BER floors 1e-9, one design up to 1e-7; reported 20 to 12.5 pJ/bit. 200G model: 113 GBd, <23 dB Tx limit, 22 dB sensitivity, 30 dB planned cabled path, <12 dB CPO path.
assumptions: 100G and 200G use different evidence classes; 200G assumes stated CWDM4, FEC, channel and receiver conditions.
limitations: 100G is preliminary system evidence; 200G is not a measured production or multi-vendor result. CPO power is cited second-hand and not matched.
relevance: Operator-side LPO countercase and loss-boundary input for deciding whether 102.4T switches require NPO or CPO.
notes: DOI: 10.1364/OFC.2024.W4H.3. Complete three-page paper reviewed; retain the measured-versus-modeled split.

title: Performance Limitations and Optimizations of Linear Driver Optics for 200G/Lane and beyond
author: Jianying Zhou, Lei Xin, and Jin Hong
technology_area: LPO; 200G per lane; CTLE; electrical channel loss
main_claim: A VPI model shows TFLN plus enhanced CTLE can meet the paper's 200G-lane signal-quality target at 31 dB channel loss, while the SiP path remains poorer.
important_numbers: 112 GBd PAM4 over 500 m; TFLN 31 dB: 2.1 dB TDECQ, 3.1 dB ER, -4.5 dBm Rx OMA and model-limited BER below 1e-6; 90 GHz TFLN MZM and 84 GHz/15 dB-peaked driver.
assumptions: Simulation assumes specified host equalisation, FEC, channel loss, modulator bandwidth and device model; BER below 1e-6 is model-limited.
limitations: No measured complete link. SiP BER language differs between body and conclusion, so do not use it as a precise comparative fact.
relevance: Technology countercase for the 200G-per-lane LPO alternative to NPO and CPO.
notes: DOI: 10.1364/OFC.2025.M2H.1. Complete three-page paper reviewed; 31 dB is not a universal LPO threshold.

title: How NPO May Fit in IEEE 400GPL
author: Guangcan Mi; Xiang He
technology_area: NPO; 400G per lane; electrical interface; interoperability
main_claim: Huawei proposes that IEEE 400GPL consider an optional ultra-short electrical attachment-unit interface for replaceable NPO modules at 400G per lane.
important_numbers: Optional single-, two- and four-lane 400 Gb/s attachment-unit interfaces proposed; no electrical performance or channel-loss number is specified in this contribution.
assumptions: Proposal assumes an exposed, replaceable host-to-NPO electrical boundary; the name and objectives are explicitly open for Task Force discussion.
limitations: Not an adopted standard, device demonstration, measured link, customer qualification or production evidence; the supporter list is not evidence of product commitment.
relevance: Defines why NPO could preserve an interoperable replaceable-module boundary where CPO does not.
notes: Full 12-page PDF visually inspected and text-extracted. Title/author/date metadata corrected from source content. Treat as a Huawei proposal, not IEEE consensus.

title: Management of External Light Sources and Co-Packaged Optical Engines
author: Eric Bernier et al.
company: OIF contributors: Huawei; Cisco; Marvell; Ranovus
technology_area: CPO; external light source; ELSFP; management; serviceability
main_claim: OIF recommends that a host-board controller jointly manage external light sources and co-packaged optical engines, because external laser resources are outside the OE.
important_numbers: A 3.2T OE can have 4 or 8 CW-light input ports; an ELSFP has up to 16 CW-light output ports; near-term deployments were envisaged with one ELS powering one or two OEs.
assumptions: Architecture assumes CMIS-capable OEs/ELSs, host-controlled connectivity map, and defined light-source/OE capability requirements.
limitations: Informative paper, not binding OIF agreement, field-reliability/repair data, an interoperability proof, product qualification or deployment result.
relevance: Clarifies that ELSFP can make the laser resource manageable/replaceable but adds a host-control and fibre-distribution dependency.
notes: Full 20-page PDF visually inspected and text-extracted. The source uses external light source (ELS), not merely 'external laser'; preserve that boundary.

title: Next Generation CEI-224G Framework
author: OIF
technology_area: 224G electrical interfaces; LPO; NPO; CPO; optical-engine placement; electrical channel
main_claim: OIF identifies 224 Gb/s-per-lane application spaces and explicitly maps die-to-OE, chip-to-nearby-OE and chip-to-module boundaries, while stating that the framework does not define a specific technical solution or priority.
important_numbers: 224 Gb/s/lane; historical 224G insertion-loss TBD; die-to-OE typically <50 mm; nearby-OE <150 mm PCB trace; chip-to-module can exceed 200 mm host trace plus connector and >=20 mm module trace.
assumptions: The framework is a consensus context document; its dimensions are application examples and its historical 224G loss/BER values remain TBD.
limitations: Not an adopted 224G implementation agreement, measured link, product qualification, production result, yield, margin or adoption forecast.
relevance: Primary topology anchor for why short electrical boundaries can favour NPO/CPO while linear chip-to-OE links remain a possible LPO/NPO/VSR path.
notes: Canonical PDF: https://www.oiforum.com/wp-content/uploads/OIF-FD-CEI-224G-01.0.pdf. Full 38-page PDF preserved and reviewed.

title: IEEE P802.3dj Key Motions — 200G/lane electrical baseline
author: IEEE 802.3 P802.3dj Task Force
technology_area: 200G/lane electrical interfaces; C2C; C2M; backplane; copper cable; insertion loss
main_claim: IEEE P802.3dj records adoption of a 200G/lane PMA baseline and a die-to-die insertion-loss objective of <=40 dB at 53.125 GHz for the listed 200G/lane copper and backplane PHYs.
important_numbers: 200 Gb/s/lane; <=40 dB at 53.125 GHz; DER0 allocation 2.67e-5 for higher-loss AUIs in the cited motion.
assumptions: These are task-force baselines and motions with defined endpoints and FEC/BER context; they are not a 400G/lane LPO channel budget.
limitations: Not a shipped-system result, final ratified 400G/lane standard, production qualification, yield, serviceability or economic proof.
relevance: Provides a standards-level 200G/lane anchor and prevents the 400G/lane paper's 106 GHz model from being treated as an adopted IEEE requirement.
notes: Canonical PDF: https://www.ieee802.org/3/dj/projdoc/KeyMotions_3dj_240516.pdf. The public 400G/lane study group remains separate; monitor it for a future adopted 400G/lane electrical budget.

title: IEEE 802.3 400GPL Study-Group Objectives
author: IEEE 802.3 400 Gb/s/lane Signaling Study Group
technology_area: 400G/lane; AUI; C2C; C2M; SMF; twinax; interoperability
main_claim: The 400GPL objectives include optional single-lane 400 Gb/s attachment-unit interfaces for chip-to-module and chip-to-chip applications, plus 500 m SMF and 1 m twin-axial copper objectives.
important_numbers: 400 Gb/s single lane; optional C2M/C2C AUI; >=500 m one-pair SMF; >=1 m twinax; BER >=10^-13 at MAC/PLS service interface.
assumptions: Objectives are study-group/project inputs; the IEEE page reports PAR/CSD approval in July 2026, but no ratified standard or electrical insertion-loss budget is supplied in the reviewed document.
limitations: Not a measured end-to-end link, compliance specification, FEC/channel-loss budget, production qualification, yield, serviceability or economic proof; optional AUI does not imply CPO adoption.
relevance: Current standards-process anchor for the 400G/lane boundary and for preserving C2M/C2C implementation optionality across LPO, NPO and CPO.
notes: Canonical PDF: https://www.ieee802.org/3/400GPL/public/project_docs/400GPL_Objectives_260610.pdf. Study-group context: https://www.ieee802.org/3/400GPL/index.html.

title: MOSAIC: Breaking the Optics versus Copper Trade-off with a Wide-and-Slow Architecture and MicroLEDs
author: Kaoutar Benyahya et al.
technology_area: MicroLED; wide-and-slow; imaging fibre; optical switching; CPO alternative
main_claim: The paper reports an end-to-end 100-channel microLED prototype and evaluates an 800 Gb/s wide-and-slow link as a potential alternative to narrow-and-fast laser links.
important_numbers: 100 channels at 2 Gb/s over 20 m; 1.6 Gb/s over 30 m; modeled 800 Gb/s pluggable at 2 Gb/s/channel over 50 m
assumptions: Prototype measurements are separated from production-module and system-scale simulations.
limitations: The 800 Gb/s module, power, FIT, cost and ecosystem claims are modeled or projected; the paper is not a shipping CPO or transceiver qualification report.
relevance: Keeps the thesis from treating laser-based CPO as the only route to lower-power scale-out optical connectivity.
notes: 14-page ACM author copy; title page and full text verified. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3718958.3750510

title: 200G LPO: Design Challenges and Latest Test Data
author: E. M. Kimber and E. Frlan
technology_area: LPO; 200G per lane; design; testing
main_claim: A 200G LPO model reaches a 26 dB die-to-die channel under stated equalisation and return-loss conditions; the paper describes module and host complexity rather than a zero-power linear module.
important_numbers: Internal 1.6T LPO estimate <10 W; retimed expectation about 20 W at 2 nm and up to 25 W at 3 nm. 200G model: 106.25 GBd, 26 dB, -10 dB return loss and BER below 1e-6 with stated TP1a FFE.
assumptions: Power and 200G performance are internal simulation/estimate boundaries with stated blocks and host equalisation.
limitations: No matched measured 200G multi-vendor system. Claimed 100G deployment and BER outcomes are indirect citations, not independently described field evidence.
relevance: Design-method and interoperability reference for the 200G-per-lane LPO alternative.
notes: OFC 2026 paper M2B.1. Complete four-page paper reviewed; keep modeled and cited deployment claims separate.

title: 400G/lane for Linear-drive Optics Applications
author: Jianying Zhou et al.
technology_area: LPO; 400G per lane; linear-drive optics
main_claim: The paper measures 160/180 GBd component operation and models a 212.5 GBd 400G-lane implementation that meets its targets only to 12 dB B2B loss at 106 GHz.
important_numbers: Measured: 160 GBd KP4, 3.7 dB TDECQ; 180 GBd KP4 plus Hamming, 1.9 dB TDECQ with 23 FFE plus 1 DFE. Modeled 212.5 GBd: <=12 dB B2B passes, 15 dB fails TDECQ/BER targets.
assumptions: 212.5 GBd conclusion is a VPI model with stated equalisation, CTLE and channel assumptions.
limitations: No measured 212.5 GBd or end-to-end 400G/lane link; supports shortened NPO/CPO electrical path, not established conventional 400G LPO.
relevance: Forward technical boundary for whether linear-drive optics can defer NPO or CPO and how electrical reach constrains the form factor.
notes: DOI: 10.1364/OFC.2026.Th1C.3. Complete three-page paper reviewed after verified replacement of defective one-page print.

title: Electronic-Photonic Co-Optimization of Linear Drive Laser-Forwarded Coherent Silicon Photonic Transmitters for Co-Packaged Optical (CPO) Links
author: Antroy Roy Chowdhury, Wahid Rahman, and Vladimir Stojanovic
technology_area: CPO; coherent links; electronic-photonic co-design; linear drive
main_claim: A bandwidth-aware model jointly optimises a 224 Gb/s O-band QAM-16 coherent transmitter's driver, MZM, external-laser split and host-SerDes equalisation assumptions.
important_numbers: Detailed optimisation: 2.27 pJ/bit unequalised, 1.63 pJ/bit with 1-tap Tx FFE and 1.35 pJ/bit with 1-tap DFE; abstract rounds these to 2, 1.4 and 1.2 pJ/bit. Model assumes 56 GSym/s PAM4 inputs, 10% laser wall-plug efficiency, 3 dB link margin and KP4 pre-FEC BER target 2.4e-4.
assumptions: Monolithic electronic-photonic OTRX; less than 10 mm USR traces with less than 2 dB loss at 28 GHz; modeled optical and electrical component values; host SerDes can supply the specified equalisation.
limitations: Model/projection rather than a fabricated full-link result. Reported energy is transmitter driver plus wall-plug-adjusted laser; host-SerDes, receiver, bias and thermal phase-shifter energy are not included in the optimised total.
relevance: Useful coherent countercase and co-design framework; not directly comparable with measured IMDD engine power or production economics.
notes: DOI: 10.1109/JLT.2025.3532994. Full 14-page paper reviewed, including parameter tables, optimisation plots and scope exclusions.

title: Connectorized Optical I/O Chiplet with V-groove for AI and High Performance Computing
author: Chong Zhang et al.
technology_area: Optical I/O; chiplets; V-groove; fibre attach; packaging
main_claim: Ayar proposes a known-good connectorized-chiplet flow that performs fibre attach and electrical/optical testing before an optical I/O chiplet is assembled with costly compute dies.
important_numbers: Current MOLA design has 12 fibres and is described as scalable to 24; simulated 0.2 dB penalty tolerances are 6 um translation, +/-0.2 degrees tilt and +/-600 um separation; early proof-of-concept samples show less than 0.1 dB repeatability standard deviation after 10 mating cycles.
assumptions: Permanent edge-coupled V-groove fibre bond; mature fibre bundle; MOLA lens connector; active lens alignment in the current design; TeraPHY chiplet on GlobalFoundries Fotonix.
limitations: Company-authored three-page paper. Tolerance results are simulated, repeatability uses early samples and only 10 cycles, sample count is not stated, future passive lens alignment is not demonstrated, and no fibre-attach yield, lifetime, cost or volume data are reported.
relevance: Direct evidence on test-before-final-assembly and connector/fibre-attach architecture for accelerator optical I/O; only indirectly comparable with switch-side scale-out engines.
notes: OFC 2025 paper Th3H.2. All three pages and figures reviewed.

title: A Wafer Scale Hybrid Integration Platform for Co-packaged Photonics using a CMOS based Optical Interposer
author: Suresh Venkatesan et al.
organisation: 2022 IEEE Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits
company: POET Technologies; National University of Singapore
technology_area: Optical interposer; wafer-scale integration; passive assembly; CPO
main_claim: POET reports a CMOS-compatible optical interposer with visually assisted passive flip-chip assembly, integrated waveguides/thermal features and a 6 mm × 9 mm 100/200G optical engine; 400G is described as an extension.
important_numbers: <0.3 dB/cm waveguide loss; 0.25 dB facet coupling; 0.5 dB vertical-mirror coupling; 90% (1 dB) passive laser coupling; 6 mm × 9 mm engine with 4 lasers, 4 PDs, 4 monitors and mux/demux; 100G eye and 100/200G receiver sensitivity meeting 10 km LR4 requirements.
assumptions: Results combine interposer component measurements with a small assembled-engine demonstration; passive placement and wafer-scale assembly are company-authored claims.
limitations: No 400G link demonstration, production yield, Cpk, assembly cycle time, lifetime qualification, customer volume, cost or margin evidence.
relevance: Manufacturing-platform evidence for optical-engine integration and a potential packaging control point.
notes: DOI: 10.1109/VLSITechnologyandCir46769.2022.9830432. Full two-page paper and title page visually verified; claims recorded as CLM-124 through CLM-128.

title: Fiber array attach for co-packaged optics: high volume production process control and performance
author: Paul Gond-Charton et al.
organisation: 2024 IEEE 74th Electronic Components and Technology Conference
technology_area: Fibre attach; passive alignment; process control; manufacturing
main_claim: On 30 sixteen-channel passive-attach mock-ups, four OBR factors predicted loopback insertion loss with 0.98 in-sample correlation; GLP offered a faster in-line process-drift screen.
important_numbers: 30 mock-ups; 1,178 observations; 1270-1330 nm; OBR correlation 0.98; mean error 0.4 dB; error SD 0.5 dB; GLP 10 s setup plus 2 min measurement per 16-channel site.
assumptions: The paper treats passive V-groove attachment and loopback removal as relevant to future CPO manufacturing.
limitations: The model was evaluated by reinjecting the training inputs rather than a held-out set; no final yield, Cpk, rework, cost, cross-line transfer or actual production volume is disclosed.
relevance: Direct evidence that fibre-attach metrology and test structure area are part of complete-engine manufacturing economics.
notes: DOI: 10.1109/ECTC51529.2024.00185. Complete seven-page paper reviewed; distinguish HVM compatibility from demonstrated HVM output.

title: Thermomechanical and Compression Analyses for Large-Scale Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Assembly
author: Rui Cao et al.
organisation: IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging and Manufacturing Technology
technology_area: CPO; thermomechanical reliability; compression; assembly
main_claim: A finite-element model of a 200 x 200 mm 51.2T CPO assembly met its modeled warpage, BGA-stress and socket-force targets after reflow cooling and 400 N compression.
important_numbers: 16 x 3.2T OEs; socket-area warpage 0.035 and 0.041 mm versus 0.05 mm target; BGA stress about 38 MPa after cooling and 41 MPa after compression; socket corner forces 0.21-0.23 N versus 0.1 N target.
assumptions: Material equivalence, symmetry, stress-free reference temperatures and an initially flat substrate approximate the proposed assembly.
limitations: Simulation only: no physical assembly, process distribution, repeated reflow, thermal cycling, solder-fatigue lifetime, optical-alignment or field validation.
relevance: Quantifies coupled large-package assembly trade-offs and defines evidence that must be physically validated before qualification claims.
notes: DOI: 10.1109/TCPMT.2024.3488003. Complete nine-page paper reviewed; numerical results are model outputs, not measured package qualification.

title: High-density Evanescent Chip Coupling with Detachable Fiber Connector for Co-packaged Optics
author: Lars Brusberg et al.
technology_area: Detachable connector; glass waveguides; fibre attach; CPO
main_claim: Corning separately demonstrated a low-loss 16-channel glass fan-out, evanescent glass-to-SiN coupling and a detachable MT-style fibre connector, but not the complete combined path.
important_numbers: Fan-out fibre-to-fibre loss 0.86 +/- 0.13 dB; six evanescent devices; minimum partial-path loss 0.38 dB at 1337 nm excluding FAU edge coupling; separate detachable connector interface 0.8 dB.
assumptions: The individual glass-interconnect sub-experiments are treated as building blocks for a future combined CPO interface.
limitations: Best results have different boundaries; the complete interface was not assembled, and no cycle, reflow, environmental, yield, cost or volume evidence is reported.
relevance: Useful component evidence for detachable high-density fibre connectivity and a warning against combining unmatched loss records.
notes: OFC 2025 paper Th3H.1. Complete three-page paper reviewed.

title: Ultra-compact Reflow-compatible Detachable Optical Connector for Co-Packaged Optics
author: Kengo Watanabe et al.
technology_area: Detachable connector; reflow; fibre attach; CPO
main_claim: A 12-channel collimated-beam magnetic connector maintained low loss over ten short mating cycles, while a separate one-sample PLC assembly showed small loss change after one reflow-like exposure.
important_numbers: Two FA pairs: <=0.4 dB and +/-0.05 dB over 10 mating cycles at 1310 nm. One PLC sample: 260 C peak for 60 s; total pre-reflow loss <1 dB; average change <0.14 dB; five-cycle variation +/-0.05 dB; four-connector mock-up 1.2 channels/mm.
assumptions: A PLC with matched mode-field diameter is used as a proxy for the proposed glass-substrate connector terminal during the reflow screen.
limitations: One sample and one thermal exposure do not establish CPO-package qualification; no long-cycle wear, environment, shock, contamination, alignment yield, cost or production data.
relevance: Evidence for detachable-fibre and reflow-feasibility mechanisms, with a clear boundary between laboratory repeatability and reliability qualification.
notes: OFC 2025 paper M4J.2; DOI: 10.1364/OFC.2025.M4J.2. Defective one-page browser print replaced with the verified complete three-page paper on 2026-08-07.

title: High Power CW Laser for Co-Packaged Optics
author: Wenjia Zhou et al.
technology_area: External laser source; CW laser; efficiency; CPO
main_claim: Lumentum demonstrates a packaged 1310 nm InP DFB external-laser prototype delivering high ex-fibre power over multiple laser and case temperatures.
important_numbers: 14-pin butterfly module: 720, 640 and 580 mW maximum ex-fibre output at 25, 40 and 50 C laser temperature; 86% fibre-coupling efficiency; at least 10% module PCE at 400 mW across tested conditions; above 45 dB SMSR; RINc below -156 dBc over 200-500 mW at 40 and 50 C laser temperature. Chip-on-submount reached 880 mW at 25 C.
assumptions: Single-device laboratory characterisation; case temperatures 50 and 70 C; lensed polarization-maintaining fibre; 4 mm InGaAsP/InP DFB cavity.
limitations: No lifetime, accelerated-aging, redundancy, multi-laser ELS package, manufacturing yield, cost or field data. The paper's manufacturability assertion is not supported by quantitative yield evidence.
relevance: Strong direct evidence that high-power serviceable InP ELS is technically feasible; commercial and profit-pool conclusions require reliability and production economics.
notes: CLEO 2022 paper SS2D.3, DOI 10.1364/CLEO_SI.2022.SS2D.3. Defective one-page IEEE browser capture replaced with the complete two-page PDF hosted by Lumentum; all pages and figures reviewed.

title: Toward higher-radix switches with co-packaged optics for improved network locality in data center and HPC networks
author: Pavlos Maniotis, Laurent Schares, Daniel M. Kuchta, and Bengi Karacali
organisation: Journal of Optical Communications and Networking
technology_area: CPO; switch radix; topology; network locality; system economics
main_claim: IBM models a 51.2 Tb/s, 128-port, 400 Gb/s-per-port CPO-enabled network against a 25.6 Tb/s/6.4 Tb/s pluggable baseline using VM traces and discrete-event all-to-all simulations.
important_numbers: Proposed topology: >12,000 endpoints; 4× bisection bandwidth; 41% fewer switches; up to 50% fewer first-level switches for application placement; speedup up to 7.1; application execution-time reductions up to 26% and 42.7% at communication ratios 0.3 and 0.5.
assumptions: Network and hardware results are simulations using stated topologies, traces, traffic patterns and latency/buffer assumptions; MOTION hardware evidence includes a 50 Gb/s NRZ first generation and 112 Gb/s PAM4 second-generation target.
limitations: No customer deployment, measured 51.2T system, production CPO module, complete cost model, serviceability, yield or proof that CPO alone causes the modeled topology benefit.
relevance: System-level value mechanism linking CPO-enabled radix/locality to customer performance and potential switch-count reduction.
notes: DOI: 10.1364/JOCN.451449. Full ten-page paper and title page visually verified; claims recorded as CLM-129 through CLM-133.

title: Monolithically Integrated Microring Transmitter and Receiver for High-Density 3D Co-Packaged Optics
author: Reza Baghdadi et al.
technology_area: PIC; microring transmitter; microring receiver; 3D CPO
main_claim: Lightmatter demonstrates an inductorless monolithic microring transmitter and receiver in 45 nm CMOS silicon photonics aimed at reducing the active area consumed by 3D CPO I/O.
important_numbers: Tx area 0.0028 mm2; Rx area 0.0032 mm2; 56 Gb/s NRZ open eye without equalisation; 64 Gb/s eye with 3-tap software FFE and inferred BER below 1e-12; 84.4 mW Tx+Rx power excluding laser, or 1.51 pJ/bit at 56 Gb/s; 8-wavelength-compatible 200 GHz spacing design, but only a single wavelength was demonstrated.
assumptions: O-band microrings in GF 45SPCLO; off-chip laser and external supplies; Tx and Rx joined by an on-chip waveguide; PRBS9; automatic ring locking; power metric at 56 Gb/s.
limitations: Single-die laboratory prototype, not a packaged multi-wavelength engine. The 64 Gb/s BER was inferred by oscilloscope software because direct BER testing was unavailable; laser and heater-power boundary is not specified; no reach, yield, temperature distribution, lifetime or qualification data.
relevance: Direct density and integration evidence for a 3D-CPO PIC design, but not a matched 200G/lane scale-out engine result.
notes: OFC 2025 paper Tu3J.6. All three pages, eye diagrams and comparison table reviewed.

title: High Power SOA-integrated DFB Lasers for Co-packaged Optics
author: Daisuke Inoue et al.
company: Sumitomo Electric Device Innovations; Sumitomo Electric Industries
technology_area: External laser source; DFB; SOA; InP; CPO
main_claim: Sumitomo uses a DFB section as a stable seed and an integrated widened SOA section to provide independently controlled high output for a 1.3 um external CPO laser.
important_numbers: Optical power exceeds 500 mW at 45 C and remains above 300 mW at 70 C; 25% PCE at 45 C over 200-440 mW; SMSR above 50 dB; linewidth below 200 kHz; DFB current fixed at 300 mA.
assumptions: P-side-down device on AlN submount; SOA section widened beyond transverse single-mode conditions; laboratory light-output measurement.
limitations: One-page vendor-authored review. Output is not stated as fibre-coupled, the PCE boundary and sampling are not detailed, and no package, coupling loss, lifetime, yield, cost or deployment evidence is supplied.
relevance: Strong device-level counterexample to a single-supplier high-power InP thesis; not a matched commercial ELS comparison.
notes: JSAP-Optica Joint Symposia 2025 abstract 8p-N203-6. Entire page and figures reviewed.

title: Electronic-Photonic Co-Design of Co-Packaged Optics in Schematic-Driven Layout Design Flow for Photonic Integrated Circuits
author: Jigesh K. Patel et al.
organisation: 2022 IEEE 27th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity
technology_area: PIC design tools; electronic-photonic co-design; CPO
main_claim: Synopsys presents native electronic/photonic co-simulation with automatic domain partitioning, schematic-driven layout and back-annotation for increasing PIC component counts.

assumptions: The paper demonstrates a design-flow example using HSPICE, OptSim and OptoCompiler; it does not benchmark production design time, tapeout success, yield or customer adoption.

title: Integrating silicon photonics with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technologies
author: Yating Wan et al.
technology_area: Silicon photonics; CMOS integration; PICs; CPO; optical I/O
main_claim: Integration choices determine bandwidth density, energy, thermal behaviour, yield and cost; wafer-level test and systematic yield improvement are major enablers for scaling optical I/O.
